Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
1002 AM EST Sun Nov 22 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
An impressive amount of dry air between about 5,000 and 10,000 
feet above ground will continue to limit rain to spotty
sprinkles for most of the day. Have trimmed back the
precipitation forecast accordingly. Meanwhile, the impactful
snow threat for the Alleghenies Wednesday into Thursday
continues to decrease.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Periods of rain through tonight with a coastal low before
  drier weather returns early next week.

- 2) Cooler conditions are expected next week, with a coastal
  low forecast to track up the East Coast on Thanksgiving Day.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Periods of rain through tonight with a coastal
low before drier weather returns early next week.

Regional radar imagery across the Mid-Atlantic shows light
returns lifting northward across the area. However, much of this
is likely struggling to reach the ground given substantial low-
level dry air. Local aircraft soundings show a pocket of dry air
sitting between 850-650 mb. Some moistening is now underway well
south of I-66 as skies have become overcast in the 2,200 to
3,000 foot level. Looking down toward the Carolinas, this is
where the more impressive rainfall signature is, particularly
toward the North Carolina-South Carolina coastal border. Models
generally agree on light activity continuing to lift northward
throughout the morning. It remains to be seen if any of this
makes it to the surface though.

Overcast skies will be prevalent today while winds gradually
turn more north to northeasterly. This is in response to the
approach of a wavy frontal system which straddles the Carolina
to Delmarva coast. Despite the rain chances today, forecast
highs should reach the low/mid 60s, with 50s over mountain
locations. In terms of the expected rainfall, there has
certainly been a downward trend in forecast amounts. At this
point, areas east of the Blue Ridge can expect 0.10 to 0.25
inches, with even lighter amounts across the Shenandoah Valley.
The 00Z REFS ensembles show the most concentrated activity 
crossing the I-95 metro areas between around 6-10 PM this 
evening before shifting toward the Eastern Shore after midnight.

As the wavy coastal system pulls out to sea, a cold front
pressing across the Mississippi Valley will reach the area on
Monday morning. While most stay dry, some northwesterly aided
upslope rain showers are possible along/west of the Allegheny
Front. Further to the east, the resultant downsloping flow will
make for one more mild day as highs push into the mid 60s to low
70s. The cool spots will be across the mountains with Monday's
highs in the upper 40s to 50s. Model guidance shows a more
pronounced drop in theta-e values which comes with falling
temperatures and dew points. Additionally, this comes with a
surge of northwesterly winds with evening gusts up to 20 to 25
mph. A seasonably chilly night lies ahead with lows in the
mid/upper 20s west of the Blue Ridge, to widespread 30s off to
the east.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Cooler conditions are expected next week, with a
coastal low forecast to track up the East Coast on Thanksgiving
Day.

After a chilly couple of days Tue-Wed under strong Canadian high 
pressure, the next low pressure area to impact the area on 
Thanksgiving Day has trended slower, closer to the coast, 
wetter, and windier according to the latest set of ensemble 
guidance. 

The parent 500 mb trough has trended deeper with a closed 500 mb low 
forecast to develop over the Southeast U.S. coast Thanksgiving Day, 
lifting to the VA Tidewater region by Thu evening. This results in 
the associated low pressure center to lift north significantly 
slower than in previous runs resulting in stronger winds along the 
coast and heavier precip with less cold air available in the 
mountains for accumulating snow. The system looks to lift northeast 
of the area by late Thu night or early Fri with precip ending. A 
brief period of upslope flow and cold temperatures may support light 
snow showers across the mountains Fri, but favorable cyclonic flow 
looks to last too short in duration for any appreciable snow 
amounts. Weak high pressure builds over the area for next weekend 
with seasonable temperatures for late November.

&&

.AVIATION /15Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
MVFR CIGs have developed near MRB/CHO, and should lift near MRB
at least at times through the evening. Meanwhile, these lower
CIGs will attempt to spread northward east of the Blue Ridge
toward the metros. Light rain overspreads eastern TAF sites 
late this afternoon while continuing through the evening. A wavy
frontal system offshore will favor a shift to light 
northeasterlies today. Any sub-VFR conditions should abate by 
early Monday as a cold front tracks through from the west. VFR 
conditions are expected for Monday and Tuesday with mainly 
northwesterly winds. Afternoon gusts each day should peak around
20 to 25 knots.

No sig wx is expected Wed under high pressure. Rain is expected to 
move late Wed night with the next area of low pressure and continue 
through Thanksgiving Day. Flight restrictions appear likely 
along with a threat of gusty winds as high as 25-30 kt.

&&

.MARINE...
Current north to northeasterly winds remain light this morning,
generally peaking around 5 to 10 knots. With the wavy coastal 
system being weaker in nature, any threat for Small Craft 
Advisories will occur in a limited window starting late this 
afternoon. Near 20 knot gusts are possible across the more 
southern waters between 3-7 PM. A cold front moves through early
Monday which favors prevailing northwesterlies which eventually
turn more northerly by late Monday night. A secondary surge 
moving across the waters will likely require Small Craft 
Advisories Monday evening into much of Tuesday. Wind gusts peak 
around 25 to 30 knots on Monday night into early Tuesday 
morning.

Potential for gale force winds seems to be increasing for the Wed-
Thu night time frame, first under NE flow before the low pressure 
center approaches the area, then in N to NNW flow as the low 
pressure center departs the region.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
A much moister environment moves into the entire region today as 
an area of low pressure lifts up the Carolina coast. Winds pick up
intensity early next week behind a strong cold front. This brings
in cooler weather, but also another round of reduced daily 
humidities. Another coastal system may bring wet and windy 
conditions to the region by the middle of next week, which could 
include a chance for mountain snow. This looks to continue into 
the Thanksgiving holiday with very gusty winds possible across the
region.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Relatively light winds through Monday may allow for tides to
elevate somewhat, resulting in action stages at vulnerable sites
like Annapolis, particularly late Monday afternoon. Thereafter,
strong offshore flow will result in decreasing tides Monday
night into Tuesday.

Another coastal low pressure area will likely move up the East
Coast Wednesday into Thursday. Depending on the evolution and
track, tide levels may rise once again.

&&

.LWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
DC...None.
MD...None.
VA...None.
WV...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$
